title: Two factorizations of the ringed-topos external product comparison
statement:
Let $X,Y,W$ be topoi presented by sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings. Let $q:X\to Y$ and $a,b:W\to X$ be morphisms of ringed topoi with a specified commutation isomorphism $qa\cong qb$. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], canonical derived adjunctions, pullback tensor comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and direct-image composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Write $L=Lq^*$, $R=Rq_*$, $A=La^*$, $B=Lb^*$, $S=Ra_*$ and $U=Rb_*$. Identify $AL\cong BL$ and $RS\cong RU$ by these comparisons. Define $\beta_M:LRM\to UAM$ as the mate of $BL\cong AL$, and $\bar\beta_N:LRN\to SBN$ as the mate of its inverse [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For a ringed-topos morphism $f$ let $\pi_f: Rf_*E\otimes^L Q\to Rf_*(E\otimes^L Lf^*Q)$ be the adjunct of counit tensor identity, as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]; tensor symmetry is used to put factors in the displayed order.

For every $M,N\in D(X)$ the two composites
$$\begin{aligned}
RM\otimes^L RN&\xrightarrow{\pi_q}R(LRM\otimes^L N)\xrightarrow{R(\beta_M\otimes1)}R(UAM\otimes^L N)\xrightarrow{R\pi_b}RU(AM\otimes^L BN),\\
RM\otimes^L RN&\xrightarrow{\pi_q}R(M\otimes^L LRN)\xrightarrow{R(1\otimes\bar\beta_N)}R(M\otimes^L SBN)\xrightarrow{R\pi_a}RS(AM\otimes^L BN)
\end{aligned}$$
are equal under $RU\cong RS$. Their common transpose under the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] is
$$ (qa)^*(RM\otimes^L RN)\cong ALRM\otimes^L BLRN\xrightarrow{A(v_M)\otimes B(v_N)}AM\otimes^L BN,$$
where $v:LR\to1$ is the original derived-adjunction counit. No cartesianness, properness, boundedness or invertibility of $\beta,\bar\beta,\pi$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $T=RM\otimes^L RN$, $Z=AM\otimes^L BN$, and write $F:T\to RUZ$, $G:T\to RSZ$ for the first and second displayed composites. Put $\theta:BL\xrightarrow{\sim}AL$, $w:BU\to1$, $s:AS\to1$, and $v:LR\to1$ for the comparison and the three counits. Let $d_B=(t_B)\circ B(t_L)$ and $d_A=(t_A)\circ A(t_L)$ denote the tensor comparisons for $BL$ and $AL$. The tensor-pullback node supplies the natural isomorphisms $t_L,t_A,t_B$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] with $(f_1,g_1)=(a,q)$ and $(f_2,g_2)=(b,q)$. It gives the canonical $c:RS\xrightarrow{\sim}RU$, its adjunction compatibility, and
$$d_A\circ\theta_T=(\theta_{RM}\otimes\theta_{RN})\circ d_B.$$
All these are ordinary unbounded ringed module categories; the two paths have the specified ringed commutation isomorphism, so the lemma's hypotheses hold.

The mate characterization of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives, with the orientations in the statement,
$$w_{AM}\circ B(\beta_M)=A(v_M)\circ\theta_{RM},\qquad s_{BN}\circ A(\bar\beta_N)=B(v_N)\circ\theta_{RN}^{-1}.$$
Indeed take $(L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2,G,H)=(L,R,B,U,L,A)$ for the first mate and $(L,R,A,S,L,B)$ for the second. The transformations to be mated are respectively $BL\to AL$ and $AL\to BL$. These are the node's explicit transpose formulas, with no claim that either mate is invertible.

Transpose $F$ first under $L\dashv R$ and then under $B\dashv U$, using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Denote the resulting map $BLT\to Z$ by $F^\flat$. In the displayed factor order the transpose of the first $\pi_q$ is $(1_{LRM}\otimes v_N)\circ t_L$. The transpose of $\pi_b:UAM\otimes N\to UZ$ is $(w_{AM}\otimes1_{BN})\circ t_B$, by the definition of $\pi$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. Naturality of $w$ moves the last projection arrow out of the composite transpose, giving
$$F^\flat=(w_{AM}\otimes1)\circ t_B\circ B(\beta_M\otimes1_N)\circ B(1_{LRM}\otimes v_N)\circ B(t_L).$$
Naturality of $t_B$ and bifunctoriality of tensor rewrite this as
$$F^\flat=(w_{AM}\circ B\beta_M\;\otimes\;Bv_N)\circ d_B=(Av_M\circ\theta_{RM}\;\otimes\;Bv_N)\circ d_B,$$
where the last equality is step 2. This is an expansion of the particular three arrows of $F$, using neither exchange/projection invertibility nor a projection-formula theorem.

Similarly transpose $G$ successively under $L\dashv R$ and $A\dashv S$ and call the map $ALT\to Z$ $G^\flat$. Here the transpose of $\pi_q$ is $(v_M\otimes1_{LRN})\circ t_L$, and that of the last projection, written with the fixed factor $M$ first, is $(1_{AM}\otimes s_{BN})\circ t_A$. The latter is the same counit-tensor-identity definition after tensor symmetry. Counit naturality and naturality of $t_A$ therefore give
$$\begin{aligned}G^\flat&=(1\otimes s_{BN})\circ t_A\circ A(1_M\otimes\bar\beta_N)\circ A(v_M\otimes1_{LRN})\circ A(t_L)\\
&=(Av_M\;\otimes\;s_{BN}\circ A\bar\beta_N)\circ d_A\\
&=(Av_M\;\otimes\;Bv_N\circ\theta_{RN}^{-1})\circ d_A.\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the second mate equation of step 2. No relation between $M$ and $N$ has been imposed.

Use the tensor comparison equation of step 1 and the inverse of $\theta$. It yields
$$d_B\circ\theta_T^{-1}=(\theta_{RM}^{-1}\otimes\theta_{RN}^{-1})\circ d_A.$$
Substituting this into step 3 and cancelling $\theta_{RM}\theta_{RM}^{-1}$ gives
$$F^\flat\circ\theta_T^{-1}=(Av_M\otimes Bv_N\circ\theta_{RN}^{-1})\circ d_A=G^\flat.$$
Under $(qa)^*\cong AL$, this is exactly the displayed common transpose: its initial isomorphism is $(1_{ALRM}\otimes\theta_{RN}^{-1})\circ d_A:ALT\to ALRM\otimes BLRN$, followed by $Av_M\otimes Bv_N$. Thus the mixed $A,B$ factors and the orientation of the comparison are accounted for explicitly.

It remains to compare targets with the canonical direct-image comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of right adjoints. Let $e_A:ALRS\to1$ and $e_B:BLRU\to1$ be the composite counits. By [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction],
$$e_B\circ BL(c)=e_A\circ\theta_{RS}.$$
Apply this at $Z$ and precompose with $BL(c_Z^{-1}\circ F)$. Naturality of $\theta$ for the morphism $c_Z^{-1}\circ F:T\to RSZ$ gives
$$F^\flat=(e_{A,Z}\circ AL(c_Z^{-1}\circ F))\circ\theta_T.$$
Consequently the $AL\dashv RS$ transpose of $c_Z^{-1}\circ F$ is $F^\flat\circ\theta_T^{-1}$. By step 5 this equals $G^\flat$. The composite hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] is injective, so $c_Z^{-1}\circ F=G$, as asserted. Only $\theta$ and the canonical composition comparisons were inverted; none of $\beta,\bar\beta,\pi$ was inverted.
